clue.text: Fling with hunk is wild fantasy

indicators.note: wild suggests something out of control, so the letters of the four words before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A daydream about a fling with a muscular man is dismissed as pure fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' signals an anagram of FLING WITH HUNK IS, all fifteen letters used.
explanation.definitionFit: Believing something because one wants it true is a kind of fantasy or self-delusion; the phrase is a near synonym.

clue.text: Cut up empty truce, ultimately null and void

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for cut is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to saw is to cut

indicators.note: an empty word loses its inside letters, leaving just its first and last
ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A peace truce is torn up and declared null and void.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up' looks like one verb; 'Cut' is SAW and 'up' turns it to WAS. 'Empty' leaves TE from 'truce'; 'ultimately' gives the L of 'null'; 'and' is used as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A void is an empty desolate expanse, the kind of barren land the answer names.

clue.text: Butcher divides stock in cooking vessel

indicators.note: a word placed in the middle of another divides it into two parts, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: stock in the sense of standard, as a stock phrase is a set phrase
to butcher is to kill

explanation.surface: A butcher separates the stock he keeps in a cooking pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like soup stock in a kitchen clue; here it is the adjective SET, as in a stock answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A skillet is a frying pan, a heavy cooking vessel with a handle.

clue.text: Van given warning to leave

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
to part is to leave or depart

explanation.surface: A van driver gets told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Van' seems to be a vehicle; it is short for vanguard, the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Van, as in vanguard, means the front section, which is the forward portion of anything.

clue.text: Feature seemingly holy renaissance artist

parts.note: a lip is a facial feature
pi is slang for pious, sanctimonious, appearing holy

explanation.surface: A painting's features look holy, as befits a Renaissance artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Filippo Lippi and his son Filippino were Florentine painters of the Renaissance period.

clue.text: National President meets king

parts.note: François Hollande was President of France when this puzzle appeared
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A country's president has an audience with a king.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hollander is a Dutch person, a national of Holland.

clue.text: Cracking clue in fundamental parts

indicators.note: cracking breaks something up, so the letters of the following words are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Solving a clue depends on grasping its basic elements.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclei are central cores, the essential or basic components of something.

clue.text: A Welshman, a Scotsman and an African

parts.note: Ivor is a typical Welsh man's name
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: It reads like the start of a pub joke about three men from different countries.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ivorian is a person from Côte d'Ivoire, the Ivory Coast, in West Africa.

clue.text: Aquatic bird I see leaving frozen mass, going north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means the remaining letters are read upwards, back to front
leaving means the named letters depart from the larger word

parts.note: an iceberg is a floating mass of frozen water
I see is said as the letters I and C

explanation.surface: A water bird watches as a floating block of ice drifts towards the pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving' removes IC (I see, said as letters) from ICEBERG, leaving EBERG; 'going north' turns that upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A grebe is a diving water bird of lakes and ponds, notable for lobed toes.

clue.text: It interrupts humming noises around bit of ear

indicators.note: around means the whole assembly is turned round and read backwards
a word that interrupts another breaks into its middle

parts.note: purrs are the low humming sounds of a contented cat

explanation.surface: Something breaks into a humming sound near someone's ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' turns the whole assembly backwards, so the inserted word comes out reversed in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The stapes, one of the tiny bones of the middle ear, is named for its stirrup-like shape.

clue.text: Drop enthralling pretence — some can't tolerate it

indicators.note: to enthrall is to hold captive, so the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: to drop something is to lose it
an act is a pretence, as in putting on an act

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to give up pretending, since some people cannot bear it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lactose is milk sugar, which people with an intolerance cannot digest properly.

clue.text: Length of suffering in EastEnders

indicators.note: Cockneys of the East End drop the h from the start of words, so the opening H disappears

parts.note: hell is a state of great suffering

explanation.surface: A long stretch of misery in the TV soap EastEnders.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in London's East End, where the Cockney accent drops initial h's.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old measure of cloth length, about 45 inches in England.

clue.text: Soldier secretes data about secret affairs

indicators.note: to secrete is to hide away, so the soldier hides the next piece inside himself

parts.note: a private is the lowest rank of soldier

indicators.note: about means the word for data is turned round

parts.note: a file is a collection of data

explanation.surface: A soldier conceals information about clandestine dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reverses only the data word, giving ELIF, which the soldier holds just before his final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: One's personal affairs, kept away from the public, make up a person's non-public existence.

clue.text: Troops hard to move — they've no backbone

indicators.note: to move means the letters are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: Soldiers find a hard place to march, and are called spineless.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthropods such as insects and crabs are invertebrates, with an exoskeleton instead of a spine.

clue.text: Test elastic bra and top on one running

indicators.note: elastic stretches out of shape, so the letters are pulled into another order

parts.note: I is the roman numeral one
on means running, as a tap or engine is on

explanation.surface: A trial of a stretchy bra and top worn by a runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elastic' rearranges only the two garments; 'running' means switched on, like a tap, not jogging.
explanation.definitionFit: Probation is a trial period in which someone is tested before being confirmed.

clue.text: Dope employed by ministry of external affairs?

parts.note: to be in a firm is to be employed by it
FO is the Foreign Office, Britain's ministry for overseas affairs

explanation.surface: A drug used by a foreign ministry, perhaps in spycraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like a drug or a fool; here it is slang for inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for information, the inside story.

clue.text: Old fruit beneath Bullingdon club member getting end away?

indicators.note: in a down entry, beneath puts the fruit below the club member

parts.note: the Bullingdon is a dining club of Oxford University, OU

indicators.note: the last letter goes away, leaving the rest

parts.note: a Bullingdon member is a wealthy toff, an upper-class person
a date is the fruit of the date palm

explanation.surface: An aged fruit sits under a posh Oxford club member who may be having fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bullingdon Club is an exclusive Oxford University (OU) dining club; a toff is an upper-class person. 'Getting end away' is also slang for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer current is old-fashioned or obsolete.

clue.text: Drops not out, with Nadal covering lines

indicators.note: covering means the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: Rafa is the familiar name of tennis player Rafael Nadal
in is the opposite of out, as a batsman still batting is in
L is short for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A tennis star drops a ball that lands on the lines rather than out.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain falls in drops, so a quantity of drops is precipitation.

clue.text: Tax office

definitions.meaning: an office is a ... or responsibility, as in the office of host

explanation.definitionFit: Both a levy on imports and an assigned task or function share this word.

clue.text: Trojan's raging lust around foreign king

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the king
raging means wild and out of control, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A Trojan's wild desire surrounds a king from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raging' rearranges the desire into TLUS, and the French king sits inside it after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Troilus was a prince of Troy, son of Priam, the lover of Cressida.

clue.text: Guardian's reputation protected in explosive event

indicators.note: one piece is guarded inside another

parts.note: TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene
the puzzle appears in the Guardian, so the Guardian's is our
a name is a reputation, as in making a name for yourself

explanation.surface: The newspaper's good name survived an explosive incident.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a sporting event, a competition of many matches.

clue.text: Well fed grain — it's evenly cultivated

indicators.note: evenly picks the even-numbered letters, the second, fourth, sixth and so on

explanation.surface: Grain that has been well fed and evenly grown makes a good crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivated' reads as farming the grain; it is the definition, meaning refined.
explanation.definitionFit: A cultivated person is refined and graceful in taste and manner.

clue.text: Runs car round one Italian resort

indicators.note: round means the first pieces are placed around the next

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
the Mini is a small British car
I is the roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone drives a car around an Italian seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a seaside resort on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Curse hum during a big road race

indicators.note: during means the smell piece comes inside the rest

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway
a nation is a race or people
hum is British slang for a bad smell; BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A curse is muttered during a big road race.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1, read as MI, is the motorway from London to Leeds. 'Hum' is British slang for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: An abomination is something hateful, a curse or plague on those who endure it.

clue.text: 50% reduction on foam rubber that's light in the middle

indicators.note: a 50% reduction keeps only half of each word, here its second half

explanation.surface: A shop sells foam rubber at half price, which looks like a light offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The second halves of 'foam' and 'rubber' give AM and BER.
explanation.definitionFit: In a traffic light, the yellowish lamp between red and green is the middle one.

clue.text: Idealised notion kept up by monogamists

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the word is kept inside the letters of the clue word, run together

explanation.surface: Faithful couples hold up an idealised view of love.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychoanalysis an imago is an idealised mental image of a person, often a parent.

clue.text: Mischief-maker in German football team?

definitions.meaning: an impish sprite of folklore who plays tricks
The German word for eleven, the number in a side

explanation.definitionFit: A prankish fairy is mischievous, and in German the eleven players of a team are an Elf.

clue.text: Composer's voguish impromptu's beginning after gong

indicators.note: after places the remaining pieces following the gong

parts.note: a gong is a bell-like percussion instrument
in means fashionable, in vogue

indicators.note: beginning takes the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A composer's fashionable improvised piece begins after a gong sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincenzo Bellini was an Italian opera writer, known for Norma.

clue.text: Addicts holding party, with old lady in a state

indicators.note: holding means the first piece wraps around the next

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, a group for addicts
Lab is short for Labour, a British party
ma is a familiar word for mother, one's old lady

explanation.surface: Recovering addicts throw a party with an old woman who is in a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the southern United States.

clue.text: Game and stunt, ie a loser gets shot

definitions.text: Game and stunt, ie a loser gets shot

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union, a game

indicators.note: shot, as in shot to pieces, means the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A deadly game and stunt in which the loser is shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue also describes the game itself, which makes it an all-in-one clue.
explanation.definitionFit: In this lethal game players spin a revolver with one bullet and fire at themselves.
